tagline: Along the ridge tops through Danish and German Iowa.
intro: From exit 75 on I-29 near Missouri Valley the byway takes US 30 east, splits into a loop by way of Woodbine, and comes together again at Harlan. Highway 44 carries it on into the Danish country around Kimballton and Elk Horn, then along the rolling ridge top through Hamlin and Guthrie Center to Panora, where it turns south on P28 and ends at Stuart, 142 miles along.

It passes 14 rural towns, rolling hills and working farmsteads in Harrison, Shelby, Audubon and Guthrie counties. Kimballton and Elk Horn together make the largest rural Danish settlement in the country.

moments.title: Westphalia
moments.text: German Catholic farmers founded the town in 1872, named it for their home province, and built its church themselves.

moments.title: Elk Horn
moments.text: The only working Danish windmill in America stands in a town named, the story goes, because so many elk shed their horns in the timber here.

moments.title: Stuart
moments.text: The byway ends in the railroad town where Bonnie and Clyde staged their last bank robbery.
